samples.summary: The CRDT move branch `moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)` (moving a slide backwards to a non-zero position) is never exercised
samples.evidence: `applySlideChange`'s `move` case has three proxy branches: `moveFront` (to === 0), `moveAfterByIndex(to, from)` (to > from) and `moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)` (to < from, to > 0). The only proxy test, `slide-ops.spec.ts` "reorders in place when the array offers it, never rebuilding", asserts `calls` equals `['moveFront:ticket-2', 'moveAfterByIndex:2:0']` — i.e. only the to===0 and to>from branches. Every other move test (`slide-ops.spec.ts` "moves a slide to a 1-based position"/"clamps a position past the end", and `slides.controller.spec.ts` "moves a slide to a 1-based position") runs on a plain array, which takes the `splice` fallback and therefore cannot see the `to - 1` arithmetic at all. Yorkie arrays always expose these methods in production, so the only untested branch is the one that runs for a real backwards move (e.g. a 4-slide deck moved from position 4 to 2): an off-by-one there silently lands the slide in the wrong place with no failing test.

samples.summary: All 14 new HttpClient methods are mocked away, so no test checks their URL or HTTP verb; the dry-run assertions only re-check a hand-duplicated path string
samples.evidence: `class-b-commands.test.ts` replaces the whole `HttpClient` class via `vi.mock('../src/client/http-client.js')`, so the new `deleteTab`/`moveTab`/`duplicateTab`/`getWorksheetImages`/`setWorksheetImages`/`listSlideLayouts`/`addSlide`/`duplicateSlide`/`moveSlide`/`deleteSlide`/`listComments`/`createCommentThread`/`replyToComment`/`setCommentResolved`/`deleteCommentThread`/`deleteComment`/`getBoardContent`/`putBoardContent` bodies in `http-client.ts` never run. `http-client-paths.test.ts` (the only test that drives the real client against a stubbed `fetch`) was not extended and covers only pre-existing methods. The dry-run assertions in the new test (e.g. url `.../tabs/tab-1/duplicate`) compare against the path string duplicated inside the command file, not the client's — so a divergence between the previewed request and the request actually sent (e.g. the nested `/comments/:threadId/comments/:commentId` path) is invisible to the suite.
searchedFor: grep for deleteCommentThread / setWorksheetImages in packages/cli/test

samples.summary: No test covers `createThread`'s unknown-tab 404 on a sheet document
samples.evidence: `comments.controller.ts` throws `NotFoundException('Tab not found')` when `root.sheets?.[tabId]` is missing. `comments.controller.spec.ts` covers an unmaterialized cell (`ref: 'Z99'`), an empty body and the PDF/doc branches, but grepping the spec for `Tab not found` / a bogus `tabId` returns nothing — no test posts a thread to a tab that does not exist, so a regression that instead created the tab or threw a 500 would pass.

`duplicateTab` conditionally copies `source.kind`, `source.datasourceId` and `source.query` onto the new `TabMeta`. `tab-ops.spec.ts`'s three `duplicateTab` tests only assert the name uniquing, the order position, the copied `cells` and the dropped `comments`; a grep of the spec for `datasourceId`/`query`/`kind` matches only a comment anchor fixture. Dropping any of those fields would produce a copy that silently loses its datasource binding with no failing test.

samples.summary: `applyDelete`'s guarded worksheet removal (a tab with no `sheets` entry) is never exercised
samples.evidence: `applyDelete` has `if (root.sheets?.[tabId]) delete root.sheets[tabId]`, documented as existing for `datasource`/`lakehouse` tabs that have metadata and no worksheet. `tab-ops.spec.ts`'s `applyDelete` test and `tabs.controller.spec.ts`'s `remove` tests both delete an ordinary sheet tab; the only datasource-tab fixture in the new tests is under `duplicate` ("400s a tab with no worksheet"). Deleting a datasource tab — the case the guard exists for — has no test.

samples.summary: Author-only edit/delete authorization is only tested on the sheet root; the flat (doc/pdf) `mutateMap` authorize path is untested
samples.evidence: `mutateMap` has two arms: the sheet arm resolves the tab via `tabIdOfThread` and passes `worksheet?.comments` to `authorize`, while the flat arm passes `doc.getRoot().comments`. Every test in `comments.controller.spec.ts`'s "edit / delete authorship" describe uses `seededThread()`, which is `harness('sheet', sheetRoot())`. The doc/pdf tests only cover list/reply/setResolved, none of which authorize. So the ForbiddenException guard on the flat root — the arm reached for every PDF and word-processor document — has no coverage, and a regression that skipped `authorize` there would let any workspace member delete another user's comment on those types.

samples.summary: `getImages` has no test for the non-sheet type gate or for the non-object stored-value skip
samples.evidence: `worksheet-images.controller.spec.ts` asserts the type gate ("refuses a non-sheet document before opening Yorkie") and the malformed-payload 400 only for `setImages`; the `getImages` describe covers a proxy value, an empty tab and an unknown tab. Neither the `assertSheetDocument` refusal on the read path nor the `if (image && typeof image === 'object')` skip (a garbage entry in the CRDT map) is exercised.

samples.summary: The mention grammar moved into @wafflebase/sheets with no test in that package
samples.evidence: `packages/sheets/src/comment/mentions.ts` is new (moved out of `packages/frontend/src/components/comments/mentions.ts`) and `packages/sheets/src/comment/__tests__/` gained only `notify-plan.test.ts`; there is no `mentions.test.ts` there. The grammar is still covered transitively by `packages/frontend/tests/components/comments/mentions.test.ts` (which now imports the re-export), so this is narrowing rather than a hole — but the package that now *owns* the regex, and whose backend consumer depends on it, has no direct test of `parseMentionBody`/`serializeMention` edge cases in its own suite.

samples.summary: "keeps a concurrent edit to another slide" does not simulate any concurrent edit; it only checks object identity
samples.evidence: The test copies an existing element (`const peerEdit = { ...untouched.elements[0] }`), calls `add`, then asserts `slides()[0]` is the same object reference and its first element equals that copy. No write interleaves the controller's read and write, so nothing about lost-update behaviour is demonstrated — the assertions hold for any implementation that happens to preserve slide-object identity. The identity check does give partial signal (a read→`MemSlidesStore`→whole-array-write implementation would produce fresh objects), so this is an overclaiming title rather than a wholly vacuous test, but the property the harness docblock advertises ("a concurrent edit to another slide survives") is not what is asserted.

samples.summary: ~19 new schema registry entries have no test tying a schema name to a real CLI command
samples.evidence: The diff adds entries such as `slides.slide.add`, `comments.delete-comment`, `sheets.images.set` and `board.set-content`. `schema.test.ts` was extended only with the alias-collision check; its "canonical names are plural" test enumerates a hand-picked list that none of the new entries were added to, and there is no test asserting that each registry `name` resolves to an actual commander command (or that each new command has a registry entry). A registry name that does not match the command tree (e.g. a rename of `slides slide add`) would ship silently and mislead the agents this schema exists for.

samples.summary: No test asserts the new `board` and `comments` namespaces are actually mounted on the shipped program
samples.evidence: `class-b-commands.test.ts` builds its own program (`registerCommentsCommand(program)`, `registerBoardCommand(program)`) instead of using `buildProgram()` from `cli.ts`, and `namespaces.test.ts` — which is the file that guards namespace mounting — was not extended for `board`/`comments`. Omitting either `registerBoardCommand`/`registerCommentsCommand` call in `cli.ts` would leave the whole namespace unreachable while both test files stayed green.

finding.summary: The CRDT move branch `moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)` (moving a slide backwards to a non-zero position) is never exercised
finding.evidence: `applySlideChange`'s `move` case has three proxy branches: `moveFront` (to === 0), `moveAfterByIndex(to, from)` (to > from) and `moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)` (to < from, to > 0). The only proxy test, `slide-ops.spec.ts` "reorders in place when the array offers it, never rebuilding", asserts `calls` equals `['moveFront:ticket-2', 'moveAfterByIndex:2:0']` — i.e. only the to===0 and to>from branches. Every other move test (`slide-ops.spec.ts` "moves a slide to a 1-based position"/"clamps a position past the end", and `slides.controller.spec.ts` "moves a slide to a 1-based position") runs on a plain array, which takes the `splice` fallback and therefore cannot see the `to - 1` arithmetic at all. Yorkie arrays always expose these methods in production, so the only untested branch is the one that runs for a real backwards move (e.g. a 4-slide deck moved from position 4 to 2): an off-by-one there silently lands the slide in the wrong place with no failing test.

verdict.reason: Verified the claim directly. slide-ops.ts:118-125 has three proxy branches; the only test that supplies a Yorkie-like array (slide-ops.spec.ts:170-197) drives just `to === 0` (moveFront) and `to > from`, asserting calls === ['moveFront:ticket-2','moveAfterByIndex:2:0'] — and because the fakes are no-ops, `from` stays 0 on the second move, so `moveAfterByIndex(to - 1, from)` (line 124) is never reached. Every other move test runs on a plain array and therefore takes the splice fallback (slide-ops.spec.ts:30-38 + 153-168; slides.controller.spec.ts:19-46 harness feeding controller.move at 129-139). Repo-wide greps found no other counterexample: `applySlideChange` is imported only by slide-ops.spec.ts and slides.controller.ts, the only fake-proxy harness in the backend is the one at slide-ops.spec.ts:176-184, backend e2e specs never move a slide, and the CLI test at packages/cli/test/class-b-commands.test.ts:251 mocks HTTP so it never reaches this code. The frontend store (yorkie-slides-store.ts:828-836) has the same arithmetic but is separate code and cannot cover this branch. Result: the branch that actually executes in production for a backwards move to a non-zero position is untested, so an off-by-one would silently misplace a slide (user-visible reorder defect, and a wrong `index` returned by POST slides/:id/move) with all tests green. Missing test over the production path of a new endpoint — in lane and major by impact.

searchedFor: read comment-ops.spec.ts (covers copyThread/fromYorkieMs, not the reply route response)
finding.summary: The reply endpoint's Long→number timestamp conversion is never asserted
finding.evidence: `reply()` returns `{ threadId, comment: { ...reply, createdAt: Number(reply.createdAt) } }`. `buildReply` stores `createdAt` as a `bigint` (comment-ops.ts `toYorkieMs`), and `res.json()` throws on a BigInt, so this single `Number(...)` is what keeps every reply from becoming a 500. The only assertion any test makes about the reply response is `expect(reply.threadId).toBe(thread.id)` (comments.controller.spec.ts:219); grepping the spec for `createdAt` shows the only numeric assertion is on `threads[0].createdAt` from `list` (line 162), which goes through `copyThread`, a different conversion. Dropping or regressing the conversion in `reply` would leave the whole suite green while every reply request fails at serialization.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test asserts the reply endpoint's Long→number `createdAt` conversion, and that the only assertion on the reply response is `expect(reply.threadId).toBe(thread.id)`. That is false in this working tree. comments.controller.spec.ts:228-234 asserts `expect(typeof reply.comment.createdAt).toBe('number')`, `expect(() => JSON.stringify(reply)).not.toThrow()`, and a JSON round-trip `toMatchObject` on the reply comment — directly on the object returned by `controller.reply(...)`, not via `copyThread`. These assertions are non-vacuous: comment-ops.ts:59-61 (`toYorkieMs` returns a real `BigInt`), comment-ops.ts:189-204 (`buildReply` passes that clock and returns the comment with no `fromYorkieMs` pass), and packages/sheets/src/comment/thread.ts:38-43 (`addReply` sets `createdAt: now()` verbatim) together mean that dropping `Number(reply.createdAt)` at comments.controller.ts:373 makes `typeof` yield 'bigint' (fails :228) and `JSON.stringify` throw (fails :229). The harness at spec.ts:30-38 uses a real in-memory root and the real `buildReply`, so the logic under test is not mocked away.
